tasks.title: Replace positioning.js with applyTransform + applyAppearance
tasks.description:
Delete the existing applyPosition and applyScale functions. They translate the legacy `position: { x: 'center'|'%'|number, y: ... }` shape and apply scale separately, which doesn't fit the canonical Transform shape (numeric percentages, anchor, optional fill mode). Write two new exports:

1. `applyTransform(el, transform)` — el.style.position is set to 'absolute' on every call. If `transform.mode === 'fill'`, set inset:0 and width/height:100%, then apply rotation/scale to el.style.transform if present. Otherwise treat transform as TransformExplicit: percentages-of-parent for left/top/width/height, anchor → translate offsets, then rotation/scale composed onto el.style.transform.

2. `applyAppearance(el, appearance, { isMedia })` — applies opacity, mixBlendMode, filter (hue-rotate when hue ≠ 0), and objectFit (only when isMedia is true and the el is a media element). Missing fields = no-op (don't reset). When `appearance` is undefined, do nothing.

Anchor mapping: 'top-left' → translate(0,0); 'top' → translate(-50%,0); 'top-right' → translate(-100%,0); 'left' → translate(0,-50%); 'center' → translate(-50%,-50%); 'right' → translate(-100%,-50%); 'bottom-left' → translate(0,-100%); 'bottom' → translate(-50%,-100%); 'bottom-right' → translate(-100%,-100%). Default anchor is 'top-left' (no translate).

Width/height: number → `${n}%`. The string 'auto' → 'auto'. Undefined width/height → leave the property unset (don't write '' — let the asset renderer's intrinsic sizing show through).

Rotation/scale composition: build a transform string `${anchorTranslate} rotate(${rotation}deg) scale(${scale})`, omitting components that are unset/identity. Set transformOrigin to '0 0' when there's an anchor translate (so anchor maps onto the same origin point).

Important: this file is plain JS, no TypeScript. Use JSDoc only if the WHY is non-obvious (e.g. note the anchor → translate + transformOrigin coupling).

tasks.title: Rewrite scene-renderer.js for canonical SceneObject + recursion
tasks.description:
Rewrite the orchestrator end-to-end against the canonical shape. Goals:

1. **Single source of truth for transform/appearance**: every object's wrapper goes through `applyTransform(el, obj.transform)` and `applyAppearance(el, obj.appearance, { isMedia })`. No properties.opacity/blend/fit reads anywhere in this file.

2. **Recursive walk over scene.objects[]**: top-level uses `scene.objects`, and for any non-glyph-group object with a `children: SceneObject[]` array, recurse — each child mounted under its parent wrapper as `position: absolute` so its percentage transform is relative to the parent's box. Set the parent wrapper's `position: relative` if it has children (so absolute children resolve to it). For `glyph-group` objects, do NOT recurse via this mechanism — renderGlyphGroup still handles its own internal sub-layer/foreign-child compositing using the legacy children shape (CP5 replaces this path). Treat `type === 'audio'` as a no-position element (use applyTransform with mode:'fill' or skip if no transform — audio renderer already returns a hidden el).

3. **Update path (mount-existing)**: when an existing wrapper is found by data-layer-id, call `applyObjectStyles(el, obj, registry)` instead of the old updateLayerStyles. applyObjectStyles handles visibility (display:none vs ''), applyTransform on the wrapper, and applyAppearance — passing the inner media element to applyAppearance for media types so objectFit lands in the right place. Recurse into children: diff by id, remove orphans, mount new children, update existing.

4. **Fresh path (cold mount)**: factor a `mountObject(parent, obj, depth)` helper used by both the cold-mount loop and child recursion. mountObject calls `getRenderer(obj.type)(obj, entry)` to build the wrapper, sets `wrapper.dataset.layerId = obj.id`, attaches it to `parent`, then calls applyObjectStyles, then recurses into `obj.children` if obj.type !== 'glyph-group'.

5. **Reorder**: rewrite reorderChildren so it operates on a (parentEl, childArray) pair. Top-level call uses (root, scene.objects). Recursive call after diff uses (wrapper, obj.children). Otherwise the same algorithm — only reorder when the dataset.layerId sequence diverges from the data sequence.

6. **updateGlyphGroup + updateForeignChild**: keep both functions intact and continue to call updateGlyphGroup from applyObjectStyles when obj.type === 'glyph-group' so SVG sub-layer overrides keep working with the unchanged 47-item children array. Note: those functions still read the legacy properties.{opacity, blend, hue, position_x/y, scale, rotation, clip, speed} — that's fine; CP5 rewrites that path.

7. **Stage sizing**: keep `root.style.width/height = scene.stage.{width,height} + 'px'` so the stage box has explicit pixel dimensions; percentage transforms resolve against this box. Don't touch this — it's the unit anchor.

8. **Visible:false**: for the mount path, skip mounting (current behavior). For update path, set display:none. Default visible (undefined) = visible.

9. **`visible` on a sub-layer/foreign child**: untouched — that's inside updateGlyphGroup.

Before-state (file beginning): old updateLayerStyles, updateGlyphGroup, updateForeignChild, renderScene, reorderChildren — driven by `scene.layers`, `layer.position`, `layer.properties.fit/blend/opacity`. End-state (file ending): new applyObjectStyles, mountObject, renderScene (recursive), reorderChildren (parent-aware), with updateGlyphGroup and updateForeignChild kept verbatim. Net file is roughly the same length.
